title: Spindles and Second Chances: Overnight Memory in First-Year Students
abstract: Sleep after learning helps new memories last, but students often sleep least when they study most. Forty-eight first-year students learned 60 word pairs in the evening, slept at home wearing a headband recorder, and were tested again the next morning. In this illustrative dataset, students who slept less than six hours retained markedly fewer pairs, and the density of sleep spindles during stage N2 predicted overnight retention better than total sleep time did. The time taken to fall asleep made no difference.
